title: Upgrade k8s client + gRPC and refactor autoscaler reconciliation to cut tail-latency
creator: Priya Menon
description:
Background: The autoscaler reconciliation loop in the GPU fleet controller is currently experiencing tail-latency spikes (p95/p99) under bursty provisioning loads. Investigation shows two correlated sources: 1) blocking List/Watch behavior via an older client-go that amplifies bursts, and 2) synchronous gRPC calls to the node lease/allocator service during slow-path reconciliation. Over time we've accumulated codepaths that serialize on a single reconciler mutex and perform repeated object marshalling and deep copies.

Goal: Reduce tail latency and CPU pressure on the autoscaler by upgrading Kubernetes client libraries to a modern version, switching gRPC calls to async streaming where appropriate, and refactoring the reconciliation hot paths to remove unnecessary allocations and coarse-grained locking. This is strictly a tech-debt change: no intended API changes to control-plane behavior; rollout must be safe with canarying and feature flags.

Scope and constraints:
- Upgrade client-go (and related k8s libs) to the latest supported minor that we can reasonably backport to our clusters. The upgrade should be staged with compatibility shims where needed.
- Replace blocking synchronous calls to allocation service in the reconciler with a batched, async request path and a short-lived in-memory snapshot for fast reads.
- Break the single reconciler mutex into fine-grained synchronization (leaseMap and poolMap locks) and leverage read-mostly RW locks where appropriate.
- Add microbenchmarks and e2e load tests to validate p95/p99 improvements.
- Changes must include a migration plan for clusters that cannot accept the client-go bump immediately.

Risk: client-go upgrades can change informer semantics and object deep-copy behavior; must validate informer resyncs and event ordering in our staging fleet. gRPC streaming requires backpressure handling on the allocation service.
acceptance_criteria: p99 reconciliation latency under synthetic burst load reduced by at least 35% vs baseline (measured in staging cluster)
CPU utilization of the autoscaler controller under a representative 500-node test cluster reduced by >=20% on median
All unit and integration tests pass; new microbenchmarks included in CI and show allocation-related allocations reduced by >=30%
Client-go upgrade gated behind a feature flag; rollout plan documented and validated in canary environment
No behavioural regressions: node assignment correctness and evictions unaffected in 72h canary run
tasks: Audit current client-go and k8s transitive deps and identify minimal bump path
Prototype informer variant with vX+ client and measure memory/cpu impact
Refactor reconciler: extract allocation accessor layer and implement async batcher
Introduce snapshot cache for pool/lease reads and add read-optimized locks
Implement streaming gRPC client and add backpressure/timeouts
Add microbenchmarks and a synthetic burst test harness in test/bench
Run staged rollouts in canary -> preprod with monitoring dashboards
Create rollback steps and migration notes for older clusters

2026-03-03 - SRE (observability): Blocking — need a dashboard tile that shows reconcile duration per controller instance and a regression alert at +25% p99 over baseline before canary rollout.

2026-03-09 - Connor Lee: First PR up (WIP) for client-go bump and informer shim. Unit tests passing locally. Integration tests in CI failing with flake in watch tests — root cause looks like event coalescing; adding deterministic test harness next.

2026-03-11 - Priya Menon: Performance bench in staging: reconcile p95 improved by 30% and p99 by 28% in the prototype path (without streaming gRPC). gRPC streaming implementation is currently blocked on allocation service client compatibility.
